title: About the portal
bodyHtml:
The CFDE Liver Resource

The CFDE Liver Resource centralizes multisource liver (meta)data, knowledge, and analysis tools into an integrated web portal to enable discovery. Developed through a collaboration between the Common Fund Data Ecosystem (CFDE) Data Resource Center (DRC; https://cfde.cloud/) and CFDE Knowledge Center (KC; https://cfdeknowledge.org/), the resource aggregates liver-relevant resources from NIH Common Fund programs and additional public resources into a single user-friendly portal. The CFDE Liver Resource leverages existing CFDE infrastructure such as the Crosscut Metadata Model (C2M2) and provides access to CFDE within a liver-specific framework.

Our Goals

The CFDE Liver Resource aims to achieve the following:

  • To serve as a single entry point for data and resources relevant to the liver in health and disease
  • To unify access to liver (meta)data from CFDE programs and other public resources via standardized terminology and the CFDE Crosscut Metadata Model (C2M2).
  • To connect liver anatomy, function, cell (sub)types, cell states, and diseases.
  • To provide interactive web-based analysis workflows and visualization tools for hypothesis generation for users of all computational backgrounds.
  • To demonstrate the value of cross-program analysis through scientific use cases.
  • To foster collaboration between the liver research community and CFDE

Our Team

The CFDE Liver Resource is developed by a multidisciplinary team from the CFDE Data Resource Center (DRC) and the CFDE Knowledge Center (KC). The collaboration includes investigators and staff from the University of California San Diego, the Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai, and the Broad Institute of MIT and Harvard. The resource also benefits from scientific input and support from CFDE program staff, participating Common Fund programs, and the liver research community. The CFDE Liver Resource is supported by the United States National Institutes of Health (NIH) Common Fund under Award Numbers OT2OD036435 and OT2OD036440.
